rationale: The fixed validation comparison is inconclusive: later WER worsens while CER improves. Retain the original minimum-total-validation checkpoint. This choice does not establish native-listener speech quality.
protocol_note: Earlier assignment-ASR diagnostics motivated this post-hoc review; the assignment set is not a pristine untouched test. Exactly three validation prompts and two checkpoints were then fixed before later-candidate evaluation. The frozen rule remains inconclusive. No native listening was performed. English artifact preference is an explicitly disclosed best-available decision despite the failed duration gate; no threshold or score was changed.

frozen_criterion.scope: Exactly the existing frozen three project-validation probes per language; compare the baseline and the one supplied later checkpoint only. No assignment test samples or additional checkpoint search.
frozen_criterion.score_rule: Prefer the candidate with strictly lower micro-averaged WER, provided micro-averaged CER does not increase, and it has no severe artifact/coverage/duration failure. If scores conflict, tie, or neither candidate satisfies the gates, mark inconclusive rather than infer human quality.
severe_failure_rules: Missing or nonfinite WAV/prediction artifact or zero/silent generated waveform (RMS <= 1e-5).
Any generated/source duration ratio below 0.5 or above 2.0.
frozen_criterion.threshold_note: Broad internal screening thresholds, fixed before later-candidate inference; not perceptually validated quality thresholds.
